rv.q: Despite the talent on show here, it feels as though there are plenty of plays far more worthy of revival in 2026.
It is a strong revival, clearly choosing not to paper over the play's rough edges but to hand it to a strong cast and allow them to really bring out the best.
This type of dramatic structure relies heavily on the success of the intruder's characterisation, and this is where Orphans falls flat.
Unfortunately however, in Treat’s case, the clothes do not make the man and his character struggles to rise above his historical personality failings.
Despite the efforts of the cast, I was left cold and disinterested in the story and would rather have seen another revival of Harold Pinter's classic The Caretaker in this intimate setting.
